analysis.title: Shell PLC: Dogmatism, pragmatism, and everything else
key_insights: RBC keeps Shell at Sector Perform and raises the price target to 4,100p from 4,000p, mainly because it adopted its latest commodity price deck. The stock was at 4,038p, so the target implies about 5% total return.

Shell raised its buyback to $5bn per quarter after a strong quarter and a balance sheet that keeps improving from already conservative levels. RBC models $5bn per quarter for 4Q26 and 1H27 and expects that run-rate to continue into 2027.

Shell cleaned up its distribution messaging. It now says shareholder returns will 'keep pace' with underlying cash flows, and that its 40-50% payout ratio guide on CFFO applies through the cycle rather than to each calendar year. This follows the tactical buyback cut with 1Q results and conflicting payout commentary with 2Q results.

RBC sees room for a roughly 20% increase in dividends per share, possibly announced with the strategy update in early 2027. It is built into estimates: DPS is $1.64 in 2026E, $1.89 in 2027E and $1.97 in 2028E, versus $1.58, $1.64 and $1.71 previously.

The case for a higher dividend rests on structural free cash flow added by the ARX acquisition, a better upstream pipeline for 2030 and beyond (Bay du Nord, LNG Canada, potentially Brazil), and possible portfolio changes in Chemicals, which dilutes free cash flow. RBC calculates Shell's FCF breakeven after dividends at about $35/bbl, well below peers.

Estimate changes are large for 2027E. EPS rises to $6.71 in 2026E (from $6.17), $6.84 in 2027E (from $5.05) and $5.63 in 2028E (from $5.31). The 2027E increase comes mainly from Upstream (+37.7%) and Integrated Gas (+52.6%) earnings.
RBC expects the strategy update alongside 4Q results to focus more on the upstream portfolio and its longevity after 2030.

Investor focus is shifting away from buyback-driven returns and towards portfolio longevity and underlying production growth. Shell's EPS accretion over 2024-30E depends more on share count reduction than its peers', so RBC expects it to screen weaker on the metrics investors now prioritise.

The ARX deal adds about 16% to Shell's production base and gives feed gas optionality for a potential LNG Canada Phase 2 FID. Shell's reserve life of about 8 years is still short next to about 12 years for TotalEnergies and about 11 for ExxonMobil, so RBC expects continued inorganic activity.

M&A is a challenge. Shell has cut its share count by more than 25% since the pandemic with about $45bn of buybacks since 2023, yet its valuation multiple has stayed flat. RBC thinks Shell may need cash plus equity to make future deals work, and weak exploration success leaves M&A as the main way to replenish resources.

Earnings headwinds sit outside the upstream. Chemicals restructuring is hard going, and international gas and trading face normalising margins. RBC's numbers have low carbon going from a $500m loss in 2024 to $1bn positive by 2030 and a $1bn improvement in Chemicals, so much of the earnings growth comes from restructuring rather than organic upstream expansion.

Valuation blends SOTP and normalised EV/DACF 50/50, using 5.5x EV/DACF, which is below historical levels given current commodity prices. Upside scenario is 5,000p ($100/bbl Brent in 2027), downside is 2,400p ($40/bbl Brent in 2027, with downstream earnings near 2008-09 levels).

On RBC's comp sheet Shell trades at 7.6x 2026E P/E and 4.5x 2026E EV/DACF. It shows a 12.2% 2026E dividend yield plus buyback yield figure of 4.7% on the buyback line and 3.0% on the dividend line, against European sector averages of 7.2x P/E and 4.4x EV/DACF.

sector_views.sector: Integrated Oil & Gas (Europe and US majors)

earnings_insights: Shell 3Q26A net earnings were $10,814m per RBC's quarterly table (1Q26A $6,915m, 2Q26A $9,836m, 4Q26E $10,238m), giving 2026E net earnings of $37,803m. These are reported actuals for 1Q-3Q and an RBC estimate for 4Q.
Shell 3Q26A CFFO ex-working capital (pre-interest) was $21,682m per RBC's table, against $17,241m in 1Q26A and $17,987m in 2Q26A. 4Q26E is an RBC estimate of $15,677m.

RBC estimates 2026E adjusted EPS (ops, diluted) of $6.71, up from a prior $6.17. 2027E is $6.84 (prior $5.05) and 2028E is $5.63 (prior $5.31). These are RBC forecasts, not company-reported figures. 2025A was $3.11.
RBC estimates 2026E CFPS (diluted) at $12.10, against a prior $10.92. 2027E is $11.29 (prior $9.81) and 2028E is $10.85 (prior $10.39).
RBC raises 2026E adjusted net income by 7.2% to $37,803m, 2027E by 31.0% to $36,584m and 2028E by 2.5% to $28,508m. 2026E CFFO is raised 9.4% to $68,214m and capex 10.1% to $23,213m.

RBC sees 2026E divisional earnings (RBC estimates) of Upstream $12,994m (+12.6% on prior), Integrated Gas $10,832m (+8.8%) and Products $10,754m. Chemicals is forecast at +$575m and Renewables and Energy Solutions at +$697m.
RBC forecasts 2026E gearing ex-leases at -0.6%, turning net cash, with -3.9% in 2027E and -6.7% in 2028E. Net debt ex-leases is forecast at -$1,203m in 2026E.
RBC forecasts 2026E production at 2,705 kboed, rising to 3,171 kboed in 2027E and 3,381 kboed in 2028E, with ARX supporting the step up.

risk_factors: Overcapacity in LNG, since Shell is involved in multiple growth projects while also being the largest LNG supplier globally.
Sustained weakness in US gas prices, which constrains the profitability of gas drilling in the US.
Security risk in key areas of the Middle East and North Africa where Shell is highly exposed.
Fiscal risk and regulatory uncertainty in oil and gas.
Execution risk on M&A, given limited options and an increasingly competitive market for direct access deals.
Chemicals restructuring is facing challenging market conditions, and international gas and trading margins are expected to normalise from elevated levels.
Resource price fluctuations, political and security risk, execution risk, and environmental and permitting risks apply to all international integrated oil companies.

tension_points.bull_case: Another strong quarter, a robust and improving balance sheet, a $5bn quarterly buyback expected to run into 2027, and structural free cash flow from ARX that supports a dividend increase of about 20%. FCF breakeven after dividends is about $35/bbl, well below peers.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor focus is moving from buybacks to portfolio longevity and production growth, where Shell screens weaker. Reserve life is about 8 years, earnings growth leans on restructuring Chemicals and low carbon, and M&A is hard with a flat valuation multiple.
tension_points.what_invalidates: RBC's downside case of $40/bbl Brent in 2027 with near-recession downstream earnings would cut its valuation to 2,400p. The strategy update with 4Q results is the stated test of the upstream longevity story.

theme_stances.key_argument: ARX free cash flow, a better upstream pipeline and possible Chemicals portfolio change support a materially higher absolute dividend of about 20% more per share.
theme_stances.evidence: Another strong quarter for Shell adds to a robust balance sheet

theme_stances.key_argument: Shell's reserve life is short against peers and its earnings growth relies on restructuring and buybacks rather than organic upstream expansion.
theme_stances.evidence: Shell needs more of a growth story beyond
